gloss: shoulder wrap; shawl; shoulder bag (item slung over the shoulder)

definitions.gloss: a shawl or wrap worn over the shoulders; (also) something designed to be slung over the shoulder, such as a shoulder bag
definitions.explanation: Originally a piece of cloth such as a shawl draped over the shoulders for warmth. Extended in compounds to mean 'worn over the shoulder,' as in {肩掛|かたか}けカバン ('shoulder bag').

examples.japanese: {肩掛|かたか}けを{羽織|はお}る。
{寒|さむ}いので{肩掛|かたか}けを{貸|か}してもらった。
examples.english: It was cold, so I was lent a shawl.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{肩掛|かたか}けカバンを{提|さ}げて{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: She went out carrying a shoulder bag.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{編|あ}みかけの{肩掛|かたか}けを、{孫|まご}のために{丁寧|ていねい}に{仕上|しあ}げた。
examples.english: Grandmother carefully finished the half-knitted shawl for her grandchild.

notes:
Nominalization of the verb {肩|かた}に{掛|か}ける ('to hang on the shoulder'). Usable both as a standalone noun (a shawl) and as the first element of compounds meaning 'shoulder-worn' ({肩掛|かたか}けカバン, {肩掛|かたか}けバッグ).

USAGE:
As a standalone noun, {肩掛|かたか}け refers to a shawl — a rectangular or wrap-style piece of cloth draped over the shoulders for warmth. The ショール (shawl) loanword has largely taken over in fashion contexts, so {肩掛|かたか}け is now somewhat old-fashioned when used alone. In compound form ({肩掛|かたか}けカバン), it remains current.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肩掛|かたか}けを{羽織|はお}る: to throw on a shawl
- {肩掛|かたか}けを{掛|か}ける: to put a shawl over one's shoulders
- {肩掛|かたか}けカバン: shoulder bag
- {肩掛|かたか}けバッグ: shoulder bag (using katakana loanword)
- {毛織|けお}りの{肩掛|かたか}け: a woolen shawl
- {編|あ}みかけの{肩掛|かたか}け: a half-knitted shawl

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ショール: shawl — loanword, more common in modern fashion vocabulary
- {肩|かた}{布|ぬの}: shoulder cloth — rare, literal term
- {膝掛|ひざか}け: lap blanket — same pattern for the lap
- {首|くび}{巻|ま}き: muffler; scarf — worn around the neck
- マフラー: muffler; scarf — loanword
- {肩|かた}{紐|ひも}: shoulder strap — the strap itself

REGISTER:
As a standalone noun for a shawl, {肩掛|かたか}け has a slightly old-fashioned, homely feel and is often associated with hand-knitted items. The compound {肩掛|かたか}けカバン remains a fully current word in everyday speech.
